Every gallery page carries tags on five axes at once. The **Categories** panel on
the [gallery](gallery.qmd) groups them by axis — click a tag to filter, click
*Categories* to clear. This page defines every code those tags use.

| Axis | Prefix | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| [**Section**](#section-the-physical-domain) | `sec:` | Catalog section — the physical domain |
| [**Structure**](#structure-the-mathematical-shape) | `struct:` | Mathematical structure — *the axis to filter on if you want to reuse code* |
| [**Tier**](#tier-standing-in-the-literature) | `tier:` | Standing in the literature |
| [**Data**](#data-provenance-of-the-dataset) | `data:` | Provenance tier of the dataset |
| [**Phase**](#phase-the-phase-system) | `phase:` | Phase system |

Section and structure codes are the two you will use most. Two pages sharing a
structure code are solved by nearly the same pymrm code even when their physics
is unrelated — that is the intended route to reuse.

---

## Section — the physical domain

This is the browsing axis: the catalog is divided into ten sections by physical
domain. The catalog ID of every page begins with its section letter (`A1.1`,
`D2.2`, `J3.4`). Only the sections that already have a page appear in the gallery
filter panel.

| # | Section | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | Transport & closure relations | Dispersion, mass/heat transfer coefficients, pressure drop, effective properties, diffusion models |
| **B** | Catalyst particle & intraparticle transport | Thiele/effectiveness, pore models, deactivation, non-catalytic conversion |
| **C** | Reaction kinetics | LHHW, microkinetics, named industrial rate laws |
| **D** | Fixed / packed bed reactors | 1D–2D, pseudo-homogeneous → heterogeneous, runaway, dynamics |
| **E** | Fluidised beds | Bubbling, turbulent, circulating, spouted |
| **F** | Gas–liquid & slurry reactors | Bubble columns, stirred tanks, airlift, slurry FT |
| **G** | Three-phase packed beds | Trickle bed, packed bubble, monolith slurry |
| **H** | Membrane reactors & separations | Pd, zeolite, polymeric, perovskite, membrane-assisted |
| **I** | Structured & intensified reactors | Monolith, foam, micro, reverse-flow, chemical looping |
| **J** | Adjacent unit operations | Adsorption/PSA, absorption/reactive separation, crystallisation/PBE, electrochemical, bio, polymer |

## Structure — the mathematical shape

**This is the axis that makes the gallery useful to a coding agent.** Every entry
is tagged with one or more structure codes. An agent asked to "build me a model
of X" first identifies the structure, then copies the nearest gallery page.

| Code | Structure | pymrm ingredients |
|---|---|---|
| `S1` | ODE-IVP in time (batch, CSTR dynamics) | `solve_ivp`, or backward Euler + `newton` |
| `S2` | ODE-IVP in space (ideal PFR marching) | marching loop + `newton` per step |
| `S3` | 1D steady BVP (particle, film) | `construct_grad` + `construct_div` + `spsolve`/`newton` |
| `S4` | 1D transient PDE (axial dispersion, breakthrough) | + accumulation matrix, time loop |
| `S5` | 1D convection-dominated (sharp fronts) | `construct_convflux_upwind` + `interp_cntr_to_stagg_tvd` deferred correction |
| `S6` | 2D PDE (radial dispersion, Graetz, monolith) | per-axis operators on `(n_z, n_r, n_c)`, `nu=1` radial |
| `S7` | Multi-domain / multi-phase coupling | `(n_z, n_phase, n_c)` layout, or `update_csc_array_indices` monolithic assembly |
| `S8` | Nested-scale coupling (reactor ↔ particle) | Schur complement via `splu`, `shapes_d` boundary unknowns |
| `S9` | Implicit multicomponent flux (Maxwell–Stefan, dusty gas) | per-face linear solve for fluxes, `NumJac(axes_blocks=[-1])` |
| `S10` | DAE / constrained (pressure–velocity, electroneutrality, equilibrium) | monolithic Jacobian with algebraic rows |
| `S11` | Population balance (internal coordinate) | treat size/age as an extra axis; growth = convection, so `S5` machinery applies |
| `S12` | Moving boundary / shrinking core | front tracking, or fixed-grid with a phase indicator |
| `S13` | Non-standard geometry | `construct_div(nu=callable)` for arbitrary area profiles |

Structure codes cluster the catalog in a way the physical taxonomy does not: a
chromatography breakthrough curve (`S4`+`S5`) and a fixed-bed tracer RTD
(`S4`+`S5`) are the *same* pymrm model with different closures. Cross-linking on
`S` codes is what lets a researcher in one field reuse a page from another.

## Tier — standing in the literature

Rather than fake precise citation counts, entries are ranked in four tiers by
their role in the literature. Tier is a judgement call, revisited per entry when
the page is written.

| Code | Tier | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `T0` | Canonical | Named after its authors, taught in every reaction engineering course, still cited as the reference formulation decades later. (Thiele modulus, Ergun, Danckwerts BCs, Kunii–Levenspiel, Monod.) |
| `T1` | Field standard | The default model in its subfield; a paper there is expected to use it or justify not using it. (Xu–Froment, Doyle–Fuller–Newman, ASM1, Wakao–Funazkri.) |
| `T2` | Established alternative | Well-cited, competes with the T1 model, worth showing as a comparison. (Numaguchi–Kikuchi vs Xu–Froment; Syamlal–O'Brien vs Gidaspow drag.) |
| `T3` | Specialised / emerging | High quality, narrower use, or recent. (Electrified reforming, CO₂ electroreduction models, EMMS.) |

## Data — provenance of the dataset

Each page's dataset carries a provenance tier recording how the numbers were
obtained. Full rules are in the repository's `docs/data-strategy.md`.

| Code | Provenance |
|---|---|
| `tier1` | Open repository |
| `tier2` | Table printed in the paper |
| `tier3` | Supplementary material |
| `tier4` | Digitised from a figure |
| `tier5` | Obtained from the authors |
| `tier6` | Reference or exact solution, not experiment |

## Phase — the phase system

The phase system the model describes.

| Code | Phase system |
|---|---|
| `gas` | Single gas phase |
| `liquid` | Single liquid phase |
| `gas-liquid` | Two fluid phases |
| `gas-solid` | Gas with a solid (catalyst, bed, membrane) |
| `liquid-solid` | Liquid with a solid (electrode, catalyst) |
| `gas-liquid-solid` | Three-phase (trickle bed, slurry) |

## Model rank and build priority

Two more judgements are recorded per entry in `models.yaml` but are not exposed
as filter tags.

**Tier** (above) captures standing in the literature. **Build priority** captures
whether an entry is a good *first* gallery page, which is a different question:

- **P1** — build first. High tier, clean published data, maps to `S1`–`S6`,
  reproducible in < 200 lines. These establish the gallery's credibility.
- **P2** — build second. Needs `S7`–`S10`, or data must be digitised from figures.
- **P3** — aspirational. Needs data that may not exist in usable form, or a
  structure pymrm does not yet cover well (`S11`, `S12`, full CFD).

## The page contract

Every gallery page, regardless of section, shows the same things in the same
order. This uniformity is what makes the gallery scrapeable by an agent.

1. **The published model** — governing equations as stated in the original, with
   the original symbols and a table mapping them to code variables.
2. **The data** — the digitised experimental points or the original tabulated
   values, in a plain CSV committed next to the notebook.
3. **The pymrm reproduction** — one plot overlaying pymrm output on the data,
   plus a quantitative agreement metric (RMSE / parity plot / % deviation).
4. **What pymrm adds** — the improvement over the original: a relaxed assumption,
   a finer discretisation, a limit the original could not reach, or a sensitivity
   the original did not report. If pymrm merely *reproduces* and adds nothing, the
   page says so.
